Accrual accounting records income and expenses when they occur, not when cash changes hands. If you send an invoice in June but get paid in July, accrual means you count that sale in June. If you receive a bill or service in June but pay later, you record the expense in June. Cash-basis accounting waits until money actually arrives or leaves your bank: you record revenue when paid and expenses when paid.

Accrual gives a clearer view of how the business is doing over time because it links the money you earn to the costs used to earn it. Cash basis is simpler and shows real cash flow, which can be easier for very small businesses. In short: accrual shows performance; cash shows cash movement.
